findings.explanation: The create endpoint's permission check is scoped to project_id via view.project_id, but the endpoint also takes issue_id and a user-supplied `issues` list. The newly added relation types 'start_after' and 'finish_after' are now treated as the 'source' direction: in these cases the user-supplied `issue` value becomes issue_id and the path `issue_id` becomes related_issue_id (lines 285-296). No code in create() verifies that either the target issue(s) belong to project_id/workspace or to the same project as the source issue; it only does Project.objects.get(pk=project_id) (line 280) and bulk-creates relations with project_id=project_id and workspace_id=project.workspace_id (lines 298-299). ProjectEntityPermission (project.py:101-107) only requires the requester to be an active Member/Admin of the *project in the URL*, not of the issues being related. Because `start_after`/`finish_after` are new in this PR, they newly expose the ability to link an issue in one project/workspace to an issue in a different project/workspace (or a cross-project pair), which the permission check does not bound — an authorization scope bypass (CWE-863). (The pre-existing 'blocking' direction has the same shape, but the PR introduces additional relation types that widen the newly exploitable surface.)
